transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (recording truncated at 48m)
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Jin (Redwood CSM), Priya (Zenna Head of Security), Liam (Eng Lead), Sara (Product), David R. (Infra)

Auto-summary: POC weekly check-in, security items prioritized. Quick results review then deep dive on SSO, audit logs, retention. Action items assigned.

[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, well keep to 45 minutes-ish. This is the weekly Zenna pilot sync, security and tuning focus.
[00:00:12] Priya: Hi, thanks Maya. Sorry running a bit behind.
[00:00:15] Liam: Hey all.
[00:00:18] Ethan: Hey team, Ethan from Redwood. Im going to cover the perf traces and log options.
[00:00:25] Sara: Morning.
[00:00:28] Maya: Okay quick agenda: 1) pilot metrics and any anomalies, 2) SSO/SCIM provisioning updates, 3) audit logs and retention, 4) SOC2 scoping questions, 5) next steps. Sound good?
[00:00:38] Priya: Yep, go ahead.

-- Results / tuning (0-18m) --
[00:00:42] Ethan: Weve been running the baseline with the cached prefixes you provided. Average p50 latency for single-turn generative QC was about 210 ms on the hosted endpoint; p95 around 650 ms for the 2k token window. When we pushed to 6k tokens the tail spiked to 1.8 sec due to KV catch misses and recompute.
[00:01:05] Liam: That matches what we saw internally. Anything we can do to lower the p95?
[00:01:12] Ethan: A couple knobs: increase KV cache warmup, enable prefix caching on the model route, and fine tune batching. We can also try the quantized model variant which dropped p95 on similar workloads by ~20% in our bench. Tradeoff is a small quality delta on rare tokens, but looks fine against your eval set.
[00:01:35] Sara: Is that the Redwood Dedicate option or hosted?
[00:01:38] Ethan: Sorry, Redwood Dedicated — the reserved pool. That gives you more consistent tail latency vs shared hosted. Also if you go Dedicated we can pin a specific quantization profile.
[00:01:49] Priya: For our security team, dedicated is interesting but we need to understand network segregation and KMS integration.
[00:01:55] Maya: Totally. Well cover that in the infra section.

-- Security / compliance (18-40m) --
[00:02:05] Maya: Priya, you sent over a list of compliance questions yesterday. Do you want to run through the highest priority ones now?
[00:02:11] Priya: Yes. First SSO: we need SAML SSO plus SCIM for user provisioning. The legal team also wants an audit trail of admin actions. How mature are Redwoods SCIM endpoints?
[00:02:26] Jin: Our SCIM implementation supports group mapping and is used by customers in enterprises; weve seen minor schema variance with some IDPs. We can share the SCIM spec and an example payload.
[00:02:35] Priya: And provisioning events — do they show up in the audit logs? We need who-created, who-disabled, and a timestamp.
[00:02:41] Ethan: Yes, provisioning events are logged as admin events. The audit log record includes actor identity, action type, resource id, and ISO timestamps. We can also include raw request traces if you need them for forensics.
[00:02:51] Priya: Great. Retention — our default is 7 years for certain records but for product logs maybe 1-3 years. What are the retention knobs?
[00:03:01] Maya: On hosted we have a default retention window (90 days for detailed logs, longer aggregated metrics). For Dedicated and Private deployments we support configurable retention and log export - you can ship to S3, Splunk, or a Syslog endpoint.
[00:03:15] Priya: So if we want to keep immutable audit logs off-platform for 7 years, youre able to ship them to our S3 bucket and we can manage lifecycle there?
[00:03:23] Ethan: Yes, we can deliver gzipped JSON batches (or near real-time streaming) to your S3 with encryption at rest. You can pair that with your retention lifecycle rules. Also note we can redact PII fields before shipping if needed.
[00:03:35] David R.: On the VPC side, what's the recommended approach? VPC peering, PrivateLink? We prefer PrivateLink for cross-account.
[00:03:42] Maya: We support both. Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) gives you a private control plane and data plane options. For a pilot weve typically recommended a Dedicated instance with VPC peering if you need easier setup; for higher security Private with PrivateLink and customer-managed KMS is preferred.
[00:03:57] Priya: KMS: can we bring our own key? HSM?
[00:04:01] Ethan: Yep, BYOK via AWS KMS is supported for Dedicated/Private. We support customer keys; HSM integrations via CloudHSM are possible for Private deployments. For hosted we manage keys but can do envelope encryption and provide attestation.
[00:04:13] Priya: And for SOC2 evidence — do you provide a current SOC2 Type II report and do you have an in-scope list of controls?
[00:04:19] Maya: We do have SOC2 Type II. I will send the SOC2 summary and the list of controls that are in-scope. We also have a security whitepaper and recent pentest memo.
[00:04:28] Priya: Is the pentest public or redacted?
[00:04:31] Maya: Its a redacted executive memo for customers. For enterprise deals we can provide the full report under an NDA.
[00:04:36] Priya: Okay. That helps.

-- Minor transcription noise / crosstalk --
[00:04:44] Liam: Quick question on log format, do you use an internal schema or Align with OpenTelemetry?
[00:04:50] Ethan: Were compatible with OT (OpenTelemetry) for traces and can map to our schema. Logs are JSON lines by default.
[00:04:57] Priya: And are admin actions tied to SSO identity, or can someone create local accounts?
[00:05:02] Jin: You can disable local accounts A and force SSO only. We recommend SAML + SCIM in prod.

-- Risk and legal points (40-46m) --
[00:05:10] Priya: One final ask from legal — they want confirmation on deletion proof for data subject requests. We need either proof of deletion or a verifiable immutability record saying data was purged. Does Redwood keep deletion receipts?
[00:05:22] Maya: For Dedicated/Private deployments we can provide deletion logs including a checksum of the deletion operation and associated timestamp. For hosted models we can provide deletion confirmation and audit event. If you need tamper-evident proofs we can export logs to your immutable store.
[00:05:36] Priya: Good. Also, are model weights considered customer data in any of your deployment options?
[00:05:41] Ethan: No, model weights are not customer data. Inputs and generated outputs are the sensitive artifacts. We treat those per policy and can ensure they dont persist in KV caches beyond TTLs you set.

-- Recap & next steps (46-48m) --
[00:05:50] Maya: Ok to recap: 1) Maya sends SOC2 summary + pentest memo (redacted) and security whitepaper. 2) Priya to confirm retention windows and any immutable storage requirements. 3) Ethan to run additional perf traces for 6k token window and provide trace logs + sample audit logs showing provisioning events. 4) Schedule VPC/KMS deep dive for next week.
[00:06:13] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks.
[00:06:17] Liam: Thanks everyone.
[00:06:19] Maya: Thanks all, well follow up with the docs and calendar invite.

Notes on transcription style: occasional mis-typed product names (Redwood Dedicate), "KV catch" instead of "KV cache", "ES S O" for "SSO" in one auto-snippet. Natural filler words preserved.

Referenced artifacts: security_whitepaper_v2.pdf (link sent), SOC2_summary_redacted.pdf (to be sent post-call), perf_traces_20250407.zip (Ethan will attach), sample_audit_log.json.gz (Ethan to attach).

End of transcript.
